::: note
[About]{.tag}
All the experiments on this site run on an ordinary processor (Intel Xeon, 4 cores, 2.30 GHz, no GPU), in Python 3.13 with NumPy 2.5, SciPy 1.18, Matplotlib 3.11 and PyTorch 2.15 (CPU build). They are **small-scale test benches**: they test ideas and mechanisms, not performance on real dynamo data. All the numbers quoted in the [report](../report/index.html) come from the result files described here.
:::

## Code organization {#code}

The `experiments/` folder of the repository contains everything needed to reproduce the results.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `common.py` | Conditional flow matching (linear path, Heun scheme), networks (MLP, equivariant symmetrization), metrics (energy distance, sliced Wasserstein), exponential tilting (regularized I-projection). |
| `e1_gissinger.py` | E1: invariant distribution of the Gissinger (2012) reversal model, conditioned on $\Gamma$; symmetry, stationarity identities, Rice formula. Costly steps are cached in `results/cache_e1/`. |
| `mhd2d.py` | Pseudo-spectral solver for forced incompressible 2D MHD, in potentials $(\omega, a)$. |
| `e2_data.py` | E2: 2D MHD snapshots for eleven values of $\eta$ (six for training, five for testing). |
| `e2_mhd2d.py` | E2: five divergence-constraint mechanisms, distributional stationarity loss, tilting versus per-sample rescaling. |
| `e3_abc.py` | E3: kinematic dynamo of the ABC flow, growth rate as a function of $Rm$. |
| `unet.py` | Small periodic U-Net (not used in the final results: too slow on CPU, see below). |
| `figures.py` | Plots in French and English (`figures/<name>.png` and `figures/<name>-en.png`). |
| `digest.py` | Numerical digest `results/digest.md`, the source of Tables 1, 3 to 6 and 8 of the report (Tables 2 and 7 come from the JSON files of E1 and E2). |

## Reproducing the results {#reproduire}

```bash
cd experiences
python3 e3_abc.py                 # E3, about 23 min
python3 e2_data.py             # E2, data: about 30 min
python3 e2_mhd2d.py               # E2, models: about 67 min
python3 e1_gissinger.py           # E1, about 2 to 3 h (resumable)
python3 figures.py && python3 digest.py > results/digest.md
```

Each script accepts `--quick` for a reduced version (from a few minutes to about twenty minutes for E1), useful for checking the installation. The seeds are fixed in the code (0 and 1 for the two repetitions of E1). The durations given were measured on the machine described above, partly while other computations were running.

## E1 — dipole reversals {#e1}

Gissinger's three-mode model serves as a "pocket dynamo": it has the symmetry $\mathbf{B}\to-\mathbf{B}$, an onset threshold for reversals (between $\Gamma = 0.86$ and $0.865$) and exactly known dynamics. We learn the stationary distribution $p(Q, D, V \mid \Gamma)$ by conditional flow matching, then measure the effect of the symmetry imposed by construction, of the stationarity loss, and of the per-sample projection. The reversal frequency is estimated from the generated distribution alone, through the Rice formula.

In short: the equivariant velocity field keeps the distribution symmetric at every value of $\Gamma$, whereas data augmentation symmetrizes it only at training values; projecting each sample onto $\mathrm{d}E/\mathrm{d}t = 0$ multiplies the energy distance to the true distribution by 9; Rice's formula recovers the crossing frequency with a cumulative error of 14% far from the threshold (up to 65% at a single value) and of 42% near the threshold; the stationarity loss improves the residuals of a good model but fails on a biased model.

Results and discussion: [report, section E1](../report/index.html#e1). Interactive diagram: [Gissinger model](../interactive/index.html#gissinger).

![Frequency of zero crossings of $D$ and mass of the "bridge" $|D| < 0.25$ as a function of $\Gamma$: simulation, Rice formula on the reference distribution and on the generated distributions.](figures/e1_threshold.png){width="100%" fig-alt="Two plots as a function of Gamma from 0.80 to 1.00: on the left, the frequency of zero crossings of D, zero below 0.865 and then increasing; on the right, the probability that |D| is less than 0.25."}

![Comparison of the variants at test values of $\Gamma$: energy distance, control Liouville residual (degree 3), asymmetry $|\mathbb{P}(D>0) - 1/2|$ and ratio $\sigma(\mathrm{d}E/\mathrm{d}t)/\sigma_{\mathrm{ref}}$, with the noise floors.](figures/e1_variants.png){width="100%" fig-alt="Four horizontal bar charts, one bar per variant, with a dashed line for the noise floor or the reference value."}

![Symmetry and per-sample constraint: density of dE/dt at $\Gamma = 0.93$ (the projection concentrates everything at zero) and $(Q, D)$ scatter plots at $\Gamma = 0.85$ for the baseline model, which is asymmetric, and the equivariant model.](figures/e1_symmetry_projection.png){width="100%" fig-alt="Three panels: histograms of dE/dt, then two scatter plots in the Q-D plane over the grey reference."}

## E2 — 2D MHD and divergence constraints {#e2}

Forced 2D MHD produces fields $(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{B})$ that are divergence-free by construction. We generate these fields conditionally on the parameter $\eta$ in the truncated Fourier basis (220 independent modes per scalar field), which is the POD basis of homogeneous turbulence on a periodic domain. We compare five ways of handling the divergence, then the effect of a distributional constraint on the energy budget.

Results and discussion: [report, section E2](../report/index.html#e2).

![Relative divergence, spectrum error and residual of the mean energy budget for variants V0 to V5 on the test values of $\eta$, compared with a subsample of the data.](figures/e2_mechanisms.png){width="100%" fig-alt="Three horizontal bar charts, logarithmic scale, for eight variants."}

![Distributional constraint versus per-sample constraint (test values of $\eta$): residual of the energy budget, spread of the dissipation and energy distance, for the V4 model, its exponential tilting, its sample-by-sample rescaling, and the V5 model trained with the stationarity loss.](figures/e2_in_law.png){width="100%" fig-alt="Three horizontal bar charts for four variants."}

A first attempt with a periodic U-Net on the $32\times32$ grid (file `unet.py`) cost about 0.3 s per training step on this processor: five variants would have required several hours in total (about 30 min each at the 6000-iteration budget). Switching to the truncated Fourier basis keeps the comparison clean (same network, same budget for all variants) at a cost compatible with a CPU. The internship itself would run on GPU, with field architectures (U-Nets, transformers, functional decoders).

## E3 — ABC kinematic dynamo {#e3}

The induction equation with the imposed ABC flow is solved by a $32^3$ pseudo-spectral method. The growth rate $\lambda(Rm)$ changes sign at $Rm \approx 8.87$, $17.6$ and $26.8$, in agreement with the known windows. The curl form of the equation keeps $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{B}$ at machine precision ($\sim 10^{-16}$).

Results: [report, section E3](../report/index.html#e3). Interactive diagram: [ABC dynamo](../interactive/index.html#abc-dynamo).

![Growth rate $\lambda$ of the ABC kinematic dynamo as a function of $Rm = 1/\eta$ ($32^3$ grid, checks at $48^3$); the shaded areas are the dynamo windows.](figures/e3_abc.png){width="100%" fig-alt="Curve of the growth rate as a function of Rm, positive between 8.9 and 17.6 and then beyond 26.8."}

## Result files {#resultats}

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `results/digest.md` | Numerical tables of all the experiments (generated). |
| `results/e1_gissinger.json` | E1: configuration, data statistics, evaluation per variant and per $\Gamma$ (mean and standard deviation across seeds), fine grid, noise floors. |
| `results/e2_mhd2d.json` | E2: configuration, evaluation per variant and per $\eta$, "distributional" part. |
| `results/e3_abc.json` | E3: growth rates, resolution convergence, interpolated thresholds. |
| `results/*.npz` | Generated samples and eigenmodes, for the figures and the widgets. |

The files are in the repository: <https://github.com/knoel99/milady-2027/tree/main/experiments>.
